Sample Size Planning for Accuracy in Parameter Estimation (AIPE) of the Standardized Contrast in ANOVA

Source: R/ss_aipe_sc.R
ss_aipe_sc.Rd

Plans the sample size per group so that the confidence interval for a standardized contrast of means in a fixed effects analysis of variance, the interval computed by ci_sc, is sufficiently narrow, an application of the accuracy in parameter estimation (AIPE) approach to the standardized contrast.

Usage

ss_aipe_sc(
  true_std_contrast,
  c_weights,
  width,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  alpha_lower = NULL,
  alpha_upper = NULL,
  assurance = NULL,
  assurance_method = "analytic"
)

Arguments

true_std_contrast

Population standardized contrast

c_weights

The contrast weights, as ci_sc takes them: fractions whose positive values sum to 1 and whose sum is zero (for example c(1/2, 1/2, -1), not c(1, 1, -2)), so that the standardized contrast is a difference of averages of means in units of the error standard deviation. Weights that break the rule are refused with the message of ci_sc and a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid. The rule is applied to the values, so integer weights such as -1:1 are accepted, as they are by ci_sc.

width

The desired full width of the obtained confidence interval

conf_level

The desired confidence interval coverage (i.e., 1 - Type I error rate). Default is .95, which gives a symmetric two-sided interval. Specify either conf_level or both of alpha_lower and alpha_upper, not both. A level above .999999998, whose tail areas are below 1e-9, is refused.

alpha_lower

Lower-tail Type I error rate, used to plan an asymmetric confidence interval. When supplied together with alpha_upper, the planned interval has lower-tail probability alpha_lower and upper-tail probability alpha_upper. Set conf_level = NULL when supplying these.

alpha_upper

Upper-tail Type I error rate, used together with alpha_lower to plan an asymmetric confidence interval. Each tail area must be at least 1e-9: below it the noncentral t limits lose accuracy (see "Small tail areas" in ci_nc_t).

assurance

Parameter to ensure that the obtained confidence interval width is narrower than the desired width with a specified degree of certainty (must be NULL or greater than .5 and less than 1). An assurance above .999999998 is refused: the floor of 1e-9 on a tail area (see "Small tail areas" in ci_nc_t) applies to (1 - assurance) / 2.

assurance_method

How the probability that the ci_sc interval is no wider than width is found, used only with assurance. Only "analytic" (the default) is offered here: the probability is computed exactly, and the plan is the smallest sample size per group, not below the plan without assurance, at which it reaches assurance. "simulation", which ss_aipe_sc_ancova, ss_aipe_reg_coef with noncentral = TRUE, and ss_aipe_src offer, where the probability has no exact form, is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid, whether or not assurance is given, since a simulated estimate of an exact probability would only add Monte Carlo error.

Value

necessary_n_per_group

Necessary sample size per group

assurance, assurance_attained

With assurance only: the request, and the exact probability at necessary_n_per_group that the ci_sc interval is no wider than width (at least assurance). The printed footer names the assurance method, which the attribute assurance_method records, with assurance_probability "exact".

Details

The plan is for the interval of ci_sc, the limits for the noncentrality parameter of a noncentral t on \(J(n - 1)\) degrees of freedom at the observed t times \(\sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2 / n}\). Without assurance it is the smallest n per group, and at least 4, at which that interval, evaluated at the planning value, is no wider than width; a width that would need more than \(2^{53}\) (about \(9.0 \times 10^{15}\), the largest number up to which R holds every whole number exactly) per group is refused with a condition of class dmar_argument_invalid.

With assurance the plan is the smallest sample size per group, not below the plan without assurance, at which the probability that the interval is no wider than width is at least assurance (assurance_method = "analytic"), and that probability, computed exactly, is assurance_attained. The observed t is noncentral t on \(J(n - 1)\) degrees of freedom with noncentrality \(\delta / \sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2 / n}\), the width is smallest at \(t = 0\) and rises on either side, so the event is \(t_L \le T \le t_U\) for the two values at which the width equals the target, and its probability is that of the noncentral t. The plan is found by doubling a step upward from the plan without assurance and then bisecting, which assumes that the probability does not decrease as n grows from there. In 96 planning sets (contrasts of 0, .5, -1, and 2; weights for two, three, and five groups; widths of .5 and 1; assurances of .80 and .99; and tail areas of .025 and .025 or .01 and .04) it did not decrease at any n from the plan without assurance to ten past the plan, and the plan was the smallest n found by raising n one at a time.

The step of Kelley and Rausch (2006), as Lai and Kelley (2012, pp. 358–359 and 361) apply it to a standardized contrast, plans without assurance for the value \(t^*\) that \(|T|\) does not exceed with probability assurance at the plan without assurance, carried back to the scale of the standardized contrast; it does not compute the probability. That step can fall short of the request: at true_std_contrast = 0, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .8, and assurance = .95 it gives 49 per group, which attains .9499, where the plan here is 50, which attains .9946. It can also be larger than the smallest plan that attains the request: in the 96 sets above it attained the request in every set and was one case or more larger in 17.

Past about \(10^{11}\) per group the plan and assurance_attained are limited by the precision of doubles. The width changes by about \(1/(2n)\) of itself from one n to the next, and for a nonzero contrast it is the difference of two limits near the noncentrality \(\delta / \sqrt{\sum_j c_j^2 / n}\), which a double holds to about \(1.1 \times 10^{-16}\) of its size. Against a 512-bit computation of the interval, with c_weights = c(1, -1) and conf_level = .95, and with width and the tail areas as R holds them (each tail area, (1 - .95) / 2, is 0.025000000000000022 in doubles): the plans checked up to 4.6e9 per group were the smallest n; at true_std_contrast = 2 and width of 1e-5, 1e-6, 3e-7, and 1e-7 the plan was 2, 1,850, 487,182, and 6,485,787 below the smallest n (about 4.6e11, 4.6e13, 5.1e14, and 4.6e15), and at .5 it was 4 above, 1,956 below, 129 above, and 4,854,160 above it (about 3.2e11, 3.2e13, 3.5e14, and 3.2e15). At a contrast of 0 the width is computed from the normal quantiles, and the plan is below the smallest n only when the n at which the width equals width is within about \(10^{-15} n\) above a whole number, and then by at most the larger of 1 and about \(10^{-15} n\). At width = 1e-6 that n is 30,731,670,565,552.9985, and the plan, 30,731,670,565,553 per group, is the smallest n; at 3e-7 that n is 341,463,006,283,922.21, and the plan, 341,463,006,283,922, is 1 below the smallest n; and the plan was 2 below at 1e-7 (about 3.1e15 per group), 4 below at 7e-8 (6.3e15), and 8 below at 6e-8 (8.5e15). With assurance = .9, assurance_attained was within 1e-6 of the exact probability up to 4.6e9 per group.

With unequal tails the width at an observed t is not the width at \(-t\): the interval at \(-t\) with tail areas (alpha_lower, alpha_upper) is the reflection of the interval at t with the two exchanged. A negative true_std_contrast therefore gets the plan of its magnitude with alpha_lower and alpha_upper exchanged, so that reversing the contrast and the tails together leaves the plan unchanged. Without assurance the signed planning value already gives that plan. With equal tails the plan does not depend on the sign.

References

Cumming, G., & Finch, S. (2001). A primer on the understanding, use, and calculation of confidence intervals that are based on central and noncentral distributions. Educational and Psychological Measurement, 61(4), 532–574. doi:10.1177/0013164401614002

Hedges, L. V. (1981). Distribution theory for Glass's Estimator of effect size and related estimators. Journal of Educational Statistics, 6(2), 107–128.

Kelley, K. (2005). The effects of nonnormal distributions on confidence intervals around the standardized mean difference: Bootstrap and parametric confidence intervals, Educational and Psychological Measurement, 65, 51–69. doi:10.1177/0013164404264850

Kelley, K. (2007). Confidence intervals for standardized effect sizes: Theory, application, and implementation. Journal of Statistical Software, 20(8), 1–24. doi:10.18637/jss.v020.i08

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Lai, K., & Kelley, K. (2012). Accuracy in parameter estimation for ANCOVA and ANOVA contrasts: Sample size planning via narrow confidence intervals. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 65, 350–370. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.2011.02029.x

Steiger, J. H., & Fouladi, R. T. (1997). Noncentrality interval estimation and the evaluation of statistical models. In L. L. Harlow, S. A. Mulaik, & J. H. Steiger (Eds.), What if there were no significance tests? (pp. 221–257). Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.

ci_sc, ci_nc_t, ss_aipe_c

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# Suppose the population standardized contrast is believed to be .6
# in some 5-group ANOVA model. The researcher is interested in comparing
# the average of means of group 1 and 2 with the average of group 3 and 4.

# To calculate the necessary sample size per group such that the width
# of 95 percent confidence interval of the standardized
# contrast is, with 90 percent assurance, no wider than .4 (the last row
# is the exact probability at that sample size):

ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast=.6, c_weights=c(.5, .5, -.5, -.5, 0), width=.4, assurance=.90)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 102  
#>  assurance             0.900
#>  assurance_attained    0.964
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> 
#> Assurance method: analytic; assurance_attained is the exact probability that the interval is no wider than the width

# Asymmetric confidence interval: most of the alpha goes in the upper tail
# (e.g., when a one-sided concern dominates). Pass alpha_lower and
# alpha_upper instead of conf_level.
ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .6, c_weights = c(.5, .5, -.5, -.5, 0), width = .4,
           conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = .01, alpha_upper = .04)
#>  term                  value
#>  necessary_n_per_group 108
